newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up supported by locals.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up supported by locals.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on optimism among local investors that 1997 would be a good year for the market, brokers said.

The all share index closed 3.77 points up at 606.73. Price gains outnumbered losses by 24 to nine. Blue chips Aitken Spence rose 10.50 rupees to 100, Commercial Bank nine to 133, Hatton National Bank 13 to 273.

"Confidence seems to have returned. Most investors expect 1997 to be a better year," said Seedantha Kulatilleke a broker at Allied Phillips Securities. Investors believe the economy had bottomed out in 1996, he said.
Manufacturing stocks which suffered from power cuts in 1996, should recover in 1997, the brokers said.

"There is demand for manufacturing stocks. Because these stocks fared very badly in 1996, they are expected to perform well in the economic recovery anticipated in 1997," said Sriyan Gurusinghe a broker at Bartleet Mallory Stock Brokers.

Investors were also focusing on banking and finance stocks on expectations that could benefit from an economic upturn, he said. Banks were the centre of attention today after news reports said Hatton National Bank had bidded for a 40 percent stake in Commercial Bank. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
